newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open higher, properties rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open higher, properties rise.

text.p: Singapore shares were higher at the open on Tuesday with selective interest in property stocks.
"Property stocks have been making a slow recovery since last week after having been bashed," said a dealer with a local firm.

She said Japaneses funds had been buying property stocks and other blue chips. "But banks have been ignored so far." Property gainers included Singapore Land, City Developments and Straits Steamship Land.
At 0140 GMT, the Straits Times Industrial index was up 7.22 points to 2,124.45. There were 91 gainers against 33 losers and volume was a light 27.3 million units.

Topping the actives list was newly-listed Kian Ann Engineering which surged to a high of S$0.99 (US$0.70) in early trading over its initial offer price of S$0.60. Volume was 9.0 million shares. The offer was 30.4 times subscribed.
Uraco Holdings edged up S$0.045 and was active on the back of strong October U.S. semiconductor data but most other electronics stocks were flat.

STIC rebounded after falling below S$3.00 last week to a new year low of S$2.98. It saw several married trades at S$3.26 and was up S$0.04 to S$3.22. Losers included Creative, Keppel Corp and United Paper & Pulp.
